self_allowance_permit_issued.meaning: owner→owner self-allowance permit required for normal withdrawals has been issued for the victim owner

caller_is_owner.meaning: the caller of withdraw/redeem is the owner of the shares

victim_shares_burned.meaning: the victim owner's shares were burned by the withdraw/redeem call

assets_transferred_to_attacker.meaning: the underlying settlement assets were transferred to the attacker (arbitrary receiver) rather than the victim

full_theft_after_permit.meaning: full theft of the victim's settlement assets occurred after the victim obtained the required self-allowance permit: victim's shares burned and all assets transferred to the attacker
full_theft_after_permit.checkpoint: after withdraw/redeem invocation, following permit issuance

assumptions: The withdraw/redeem call is the checked action; the permit issuance precedes it.
The attacker is an arbitrary address that is not the owner and holds no approved delegation.
The report treats the self-allowance permit as the only authorization consumed by withdraw/redeem.

unresolved.description: The report does not state whether an approved delegate (allowance holder) distinct from the owner could also legitimately trigger withdraw/redeem; the authorization predicate is narrowed to caller==owner.

limitations: Authorization is modeled as caller==owner; the delegate/allowance branch of the NatSpec requirement is not separately encoded.
The impact's 'full' magnitude (all shares burned, all assets moved) is represented by the burn and transfer occurrence observables rather than numeric amounts, since the report gives no quantities.
The permit-issuance precondition is potential in the report; it is bound as a scenario fact for this claim.
The impact-context predicate uses the impact-specific full_theft_after_permit observable, which cites the selected impact ID, alongside the permit-issuance precondition.
